profile.title: Profile
profile.role: Role: {role} — an administrator changes it in settings.

language.title: Interface language
language.hint: The interface, emails and exports will be in this language for you. “Studio default” follows the studio settings.

password.title: Change password
password.why: The current password is needed even while you are signed in — otherwise anyone at an unattended screen could lock you out of your own account.
password.tooShort: The new password is shorter than 8 characters
password.mismatch: The new password and its repeat do not match

notificationSettings.title: Notifications
notificationSettings.intro: What arrives in the bell and what comes by email to {email}. Changes are saved at once.
notificationSettings.loadFailed: Could not load the notification settings.
notificationSettings.noEmail: No emails are sent for this event

settings.title: Settings
settings.readOnly: You have view access: the fields are visible, but changes cannot be saved.

studio.name: Studio name
studio.defaultLanguageHint: For everyone who has not picked a language in their profile, and for the sign-in page, emails and exports.

mail.intro: Until SMTP is filled in, confirmation codes and notifications are not sent — they are written to the server log. Sign-up formally works, but a real person will not receive the code.
mail.portHint: 465 means TLS from the start, any other port uses STARTTLS.
mail.passwordSet: Saved — leave empty to keep it
mail.passwordHint: The password is never sent back — it cannot be viewed on this page.
mail.test: Send a test email to myself

templates.intro: A template sets the list of stages a new project is filled with. Stages from the standard pipeline keep their weight and department; an unfamiliar name becomes a stage too — with weight 1 and no department.
templates.empty: No custom templates yet — projects are created with the built-in pipeline.
templates.name: Name
templates.stages: Stages — one per line, in order
templates.deleteDetail: Projects already created will not change — a template only affects new ones.

users.intro: All accounts are here, including those without an employee card — client portal users, for example. Hiring, position and rate live in {link}.

team.noMatches: No one matches the selected filters.

employees.title: Employees
employees.emptyBody: Add employees to assign them to tasks.
employees.deleteDetail: The account and its access are deleted and the email address is freed. Tasks and versions are left without an assignee; if the employee has timesheets or comments, their record stays in the database without access.

attendance.title: Employee attendance
attendance.intro: Who came to work and who did not. Arrival is a press of “I’m in” in the site header; leaving is “I’m leaving” or the last activity.

workload.title: Team workload
workload.summary: {people} people · {assigned} h assigned of {capacity} h · average load {average}%

board.dayOff: Not a working day by the schedule
board.noStaff: There are no employees on staff yet.
board.unmarkedTitle: Did not press “I’m in” — time of first activity

days.loadFailed: Could not load the employee’s days.

correct.resetFailed: Could not restore the automatic data
correct.title: Correct the day
correct.observed: The system saw: first sign-in {first}, last activity {last}.
correct.emptyHint: An empty arrival means the employee was not at work that day.
correct.reasonPlaceholder: E.g. forgot to sign in, was on a shoot from 9:00

period.unmarkedTitle: Was online but did not press “I’m in”: {days}

confirm.title: Fine for lateness?
confirm.message: For {from} — {to}, every late day becomes a draft fine in Payroll. Rate: {rate}.
confirm.detail: Days that already have a fine are skipped — running it again does not double anything. The drafts still need approval.

timesheets.title: Time tracking
timesheets.required: Fill in the project, the date and the number of hours
timesheets.noSearch: Search is not available in this section
timesheets.emptyBody: Logged hours make up the actual cost of a project.
timesheets.deleteDetail: The hours will disappear from reports and from the project cost.

activity.title: Activity feed
activity.intro: What happened in the studio: who created, reassigned and moved what to another status. The feed is read-only — an event cannot be edited, and that is the point.
activity.emptyFilteredBody: Try widening the period or removing some filters.
activity.emptyBody: Status changes, versions and reviews will appear here as soon as they happen.

schedule.intro: The Attendance section measures lateness and worked time against this schedule. Arrival is a press of “I’m in” (without it, the first activity of the day); leaving is “I’m leaving” or the last activity. Times are in the studio’s time zone (the Studio tab).
schedule.graceHint: Arriving before {start} + grace is not late. Later than that, lateness counts from {start}.
schedule.penaltyHint: The rates add up: being 25 minutes late costs {amount} {currency}. Both at zero means no fines. Fines are created by hand on the Attendance page and become drafts in Payroll.

roles.ownerAll: The owner can always do everything
roles.ceiling: This right cannot be given to this role
roles.notYours: Your role does not have this right, so you cannot grant it
roles.saved: Permissions saved. Users will see the changes the next time a page loads.
roles.resetDone: The “{role}” role is back to its standard permissions.
roles.title: Who sees and does what
roles.intro: The first row of each section opens its page; the others are actions inside it. The owner can always do everything; you can only grant what your own role has; clients only get the client set. Changes take effect the next time the user loads a page.
